observed.facings.png: A 4x4 linked-pipe atlas on a checker background, labelled 'south'. Every tile uses one orange-brown copper tube of the same width. The tiles cover: two elbows, an end-capped stub going left, a tee with a round riveted boss, a vertical run bending into an elbow, a horizontal tee, a 4-way cross with a boss, a tee lower down, a short vertical stub with a domed cap on top, an isolated tile that is a lone round riveted boss, a long vertical run ending in a domed cap with a rivet band, an elbow, a left-pointing end cap, and a tee with an elbow below it. The alpha outside the tube is clean.
observed.south.png: The same atlas at full resolution on transparency. The tube has a darker outline on both sides, a lighter centre stripe, faint diagonal cross-hatch mottling along its length, and some greenish-pink tint variation. Bosses are round domed copper discs with about 6 to 8 small rivets around the rim. End caps are half-dome caps with a riveted collar band. Elbows are smooth quarter-circles with a constant radius and stay on the pipe axis. No couplings or seams sit at the tile edges.
observed.single.png: Identical to south.png: the full atlas, transparent background.
observed.scale.png: An offline render at 96 px per cell on brown dirt. A horizontal run starts at a left end cap, passes a red-copper faucet (valve wheel), reaches a tee with a riveted boss whose branch runs down to a domed end cap, continues past a sprinkler head, then turns up through a smooth S of two elbows to another horizontal run ending in an end cap at the upper right. A vanilla pawn is in an inset on the right. The pipe is a thin line, much narrower than the pawn's body. The joins are seamless and the boss is centred on both axes.
observed.siblings.png: The top half is an empty checker panel. The bottom half is 'sibling_industrial_90': the same layout drawn with a thin dark grey/steel pipe, small dark junction and end-cap nubs, and faucet and sprinkler sprites. That pipe is somewhat thinner and plainer than the copper candidate.
observed.assembled_1.png: The same layout at 90 px per cell without the pawn. Copper pipe, a riveted boss at the tee, domed end caps on all three dead ends, smooth elbows in the S-bend, and the faucet and sprinkler drawn on top of the run. The pipe is continuous through every cell boundary. It looks tidy and uniform, like new copper plumbing.
observed.assembled_2.png: The same layout at 48 px per cell. The pipe still reads as a continuous copper line. The boss shows as a dot at the tee and the end caps as small knobs. The faucet and sprinkler are small but distinguishable. Everything stays legible at this size.

CAMERA.seen: It is flat ground art seen from above, which the card's engine limits allow for Graphic_Linked pipes. Bosses are circles and the tube is lit along its centre, consistent with the top-down pipe convention and the industrial sibling.

BORE.seen: No open bore is shown anywhere. Every dead end is closed by a domed, riveted end cap, and the elbows are solid bends.

PORTS.seen: In assembled_1 and scale.png, every cell's pipe meets the next cell's pipe on the same axis at the cell edge with no offset, gap or kink. The faucet and sprinkler sit on the pipe centreline.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: Every atlas tile has pipe ends only on the sides its neighbour mask calls for. No stray connectors or couplings sit inside the tiles or in the padding.

LAYERS.seen: The faucet and sprinkler head draw on top of the pipe run. The boss draws over the crossing pipes.

ROTATIONS.seen: There is one linked atlas with no per-facing art. Every tile uses the same tube, palette, boss and end cap.

SIGNATURE.seen: Straights, elbows (radius about half a cell), tees and crosses with a symmetric riveted boss, and bolted end caps are all present and join automatically in the assembled views. The 'salvage/junk-built' character is weak (see finding).

MATERIAL.seen: It reads as copper tube: a dark rim outline, a specular centre stripe and mottled patina tint. The diagonal cross-hatch mottling is slightly synthetic but still reads as metal, not paint.

FOOTPRINT.seen: Each tile stays inside its cell. The pipe is thin and centred, and the joins land on the cell edges.

ALPHA.seen: south.png and single.png have clean transparency with no shadow, halo or ground patch.

OURS.seen: The art is our own: generated copper strip and boss composited on our atlas geometry. It is not vanilla or another mod's pipe.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The 'bad art alignment' complaint is addressed: one uniform tube, no banding mismatch, the tee boss centred on the axis, end caps attached, and no kink or hidden couplings. The 'bad art' complaint is mostly addressed with a clean, consistent copper rendering.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 48 px per cell (assembled_2) the run, tee boss and end caps all read. At 32 px it will be a thin copper line with dots at the junctions, which is enough for ground clutter.

findings.seen: The pipe is one pristine, uniform copper tube with tidy riveted bosses. Nothing reads as salvage or junk-built: no patches, mismatched segments, wire wraps, dents or heavy corrosion.

findings.fix: Make the tube surface carry irregular, non-repeating wear and oxidation along its length instead of a regular diagonal hatch.

reply.image_seen: 1: copper linked-tile atlas on checkerboard; 2: isolated copper atlas; 3: matching single-atlas image; 4: assembled pipe beside a human; 5: thin industrial sibling reference; 6: connected copper run with tee, bends, caps and contextual fixtures; 7: smaller-scale view of that assembly.

concerns.evidence: The enlarged tubes in south.png show mottled brown surface wear, uneven copper highlights and darkened edges; the bosses and end caps have dark seams and recessed fasteners. They are orderly and uniform, but not pristine. The description explicitly requests one uniform worn-copper tube; patches, mismatched segments and wire wraps are not required.

The atlas visibly provides differently oriented bends and capped ends with consistent tube width and copper treatment, and the offline assemblies show continuous joins. Separate facing files are excluded by the stated Graphic_Linked engine limit. However, the card explicitly identifies both assembled panels as offline renders, so the class module's required in-game verification of connections and layering remains unavailable.

request.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper
invariants: one uniform worn-copper tube colour along every tile, with no banding and no grey sections
pipe width of 18 px centred in a 132 px cell, so every tile's connecting ends meet the cell edge at the same height and width
elbows bend on the pipe axis with a radius of half a cell
a round, symmetric riveted boss at every 3-way and 4-way junction, centred on the cell
a bolted end cap closes each dead end and sits flush on the pipe axis
couplings sit inside the cell, clear of the atlas padding
painterly vanilla RimWorld style, clean dark outline, transparent background
request.prompt:
A 4x4 atlas of RimWorld linked-graphic floor pipe tiles in the Scrapper (salvage, junk-built) look. Each cell is 132 px square and holds one tile. The pipe is flat, low ground clutter seen from directly above, 18 px thick and centred in its cell, drawn to sit under pawns. The atlas covers every neighbour combination: isolated stub, dead-end cap in each of four directions, straight horizontal and vertical runs, four elbows, four tees and one four-way cross.

Material: a single uniform worn copper tube throughout, warm brown-orange with soft verdigris dulling at the edges, subtle scuffs and a few patched seams that read as scavenged plumbing. The colour is identical in every tile, so adjacent tiles join into one continuous tube with no visible seam. A narrow highlight runs along the top of the tube and a darker shade along its lower edge. A clean dark outline surrounds the pipe silhouette.

Straights: the tube runs edge to edge through the cell centre. Its ends meet the cell border at exactly the same position and width in every tile, and a plain low flanged coupling sits mid-cell, well inside the cell.

Elbows: the tube bends in a smooth quarter curve whose centreline follows the pipe axis with a radius of half a cell. The elbow tube has the same width, colour and outline as the straights, and its two ends meet the cell edges at the centre point.

Tees and cross: a round, symmetric riveted boss, centred on the cell, sits at the junction. Its rivets are evenly spaced around its rim. Each branch leaves the boss on the pipe axis at the same width as a straight.

End caps: the dead end is closed by a round bolted cap sitting flush on the pipe axis. It has four small bolts and a slightly wider rim, and it stays inside the cell with the tube leading to the opposite edge.

View: orthographic top-down, the same lighting in every tile (light from upper left). Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld style, fully transparent background, crisp edges, and a clean dark outline that stays legible when the sprite is scaled down.
